newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to continue deficit fight - minister.
newsitem.headline: Canada to continue deficit fight - minister.

text.p: Canada's new Liberal government will stay the course on reducing the deficit, despite pressure to increase spending, the new junior minister for financial institutions said on Thursday.

"The clear message from the election campaign is we're going to hold the course until we have a balanced budget and a surplus," Secretary of State for International Financial Institutions Jim Peterson told reporters on the way into a cabinet meeting.

"We can't open up the floodgates. We have to stay the course," he said. "This is what has produced our incredible economic turnaround. This is the greatest opportunity for all Canadians to continue the course we've been on, to finish the job."
Peterson said that once Canada's budget deficit has turned into a surplus, the government will look at spending on child poverty and youth unemployment.
"We have children in poverty, we have youth unemployment, we have kids who have been abused or deprived of opportunity," he said. "There would be a lot of priorities."
Peterson was sworn in to his new position on Wednesday, after the Liberal government was re-elected by a slim majority in federal elections on June 2.

During the previous Liberal administration, the government reduced the budget deficit to an expected C$15 billion for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1997, down from C$42 billion when the Liberals took office in 1993. The final figures for the year ending in March 1997 will not be available until this autumn.
